newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico primary Cetes rates seen falling Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Mexico primary Cetes rates seen falling Tuesday.

text.p: Dealers and analysts said Monday they expected Cetes rates to fall at Tuesday's primary auction in response to a stable peso and low secondary rates.
"Although the scope for rates to fall has been reduced, the background is conducive to moderate rate reductions, with longer term issues falling most," a money market analyst said.
Analysts expect 28-day Cetes rates to fall by less than 25 basis points this week, and by as much as 75 basis points on longer term issues.
Banco de Mexico called for bids for a total of 3.3 billion pesos in Cetes at 28, 91, 182 and 364 days.
The benchmark 48-hour peso has been trading in a range between 7.52 and 7.54 per dollar, while overnight Cetes rates have traded between 21.60 and 23 percent.
Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 23.06 percent last week.
Traders said the fall in U.S. long bond rates following lower-than-expected employment data Friday provided an extra margin for falls in Mexican rates.
"The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond yield is below 6.80 percent, and that is taking pressure off domestic rates," a trader said.

Analysts pointed out that falls in Cetes yields could be reined in by lower demand from cautious investors awaiting the publication of the official economic policy criteria for 1997, expected in November following consultations between the government, labor and business leaders.
Future auctions could see Cetes rates rise again, analysts added, as real returns have fallen considerably.

Inverlat brokerage said in its weekly report that the months when inflation traditionally reaches a seasonal peak are approaching, and "uncertainty reigns among investors over next year's economic program."
